newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police dig for Mafia victims.
newsitem.headline: Italian police dig for Mafia victims.

text.p: Police in Sicily began digging for the remains of Mafia victims at various locations around the capital Palermo on Monday after an alleged hitman captured last week decided to turn state's evidence.
Italian news agency ANSA said Salvatore Grigoli had told police where victims were buried.
Police gave no details of the searches.
Grigoli, wanted over the killing of a Roman Catholic priest, was reported to have begun cooperating with police within hours of his arrest last Thursday.
Magistrates separately hailed their third anti-Mafia coup within a month after the arrest on Sunday night of another alleged hitman suspected of taking part in dozens of killings.

Antonino Tinnirello, 35, was arrested after police intercepted a phone call and followed him and his wife to a wood on the outskirts of Corleone, the hilltop town immortalised in the Godfather movies.
He had been on the run since 1989 and had already been given a 16-year jail sentence in absentia.
The latest arrests followed that of Pietro Aglieri on June 6, one of the most powerful of the fugitive Mafia bosses.

"The arrest of Antonino Tinnirello, one of the most dangerous killers of the Brancaccio hit-squad, is another significant success for the (police) after the arrests of Pietro Aglieri and Salvatore Grigoli," Palermo's assistant prosecutor Guido Lo Forte told reporters.
